questions.question: In a robot, which component detects distance from a nearby obstacle?
choices: A sensor
An actuator
A gear train
A chassis

questions.question: What is an algorithm?
choices: A device that converts electricity to motion
A sequence of steps for solving a problem
A measurement that cannot be repeated
A type of robot battery

questions.question: A program repeats a movement sequence four times. Which programming structure is most appropriate?
choices: Variable
Comment
Loop
Sensor

questions.question: A robot turns left only when its distance sensor detects an obstacle within 10 centimeters. This behavior uses
choices: a fixed sequence with no input
a comment instead of an instruction
an actuator as a measurement
a conditional decision

questions.question: Which part of a robot produces motion in response to a control signal?
choices: Actuator
Sensor
Algorithm
Input value

questions.question: A line-following robot drifts off the track, corrects itself, and then drifts again. Which improvement most directly supports stable control?
choices: Disable the sensors and increase the maximum speed
Use sensor feedback to make smaller, timely motor adjustments
Repeat the same full-speed turn on every surface
Remove the control loop

questions.question: A robot's sensor returns 6 centimeters, but the program treats every value below 8 centimeters as an obstacle. What should the robot do?
choices: Continue as if no sensor reading exists
Rewrite the sensor value as 8
Execute the obstacle-response branch
Stop the program before evaluating the condition

questions.question: What is debugging?
choices: Adding more hardware without testing
Copying code without understanding it
Choosing a robot's color scheme
Finding and correcting problems in a program or system

questions.question: A program tells a robot to move forward 20 centimeters, but it moves 28 centimeters. Which next step is most useful?
choices: Measure the difference across repeated trials and adjust the movement command
Change the robot's name and rerun once
Assume the distance sensor caused the error without checking
Remove all movement commands

questions.question: In a block-based program, a variable is useful for
choices: physically connecting a wheel to a motor
storing a value that a program can use or update
detecting light without a sensor
making every instruction run simultaneously

questions.question: A robot repeats a pick-and-place routine until a bin is empty. What condition should end the loop?
choices: The robot has completed exactly one movement
The battery voltage rises above its starting level
The sensor or counter indicates that no items remain
The program reaches a comment

questions.question: A team's robot works in a test area but not on a darker floor. What is the best troubleshooting approach?
choices: Replace the drive motors before examining the sensor
Change the program, floor, and lighting at the same time
Remove the floor sensor data from the report
Investigate how surface color affects the sensor readings and retest controlled changes

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes input and output in a simple robot system?
choices: A sensor provides input; a motor can produce output
A motor provides input; an algorithm is a physical output
A battery is an algorithm; a sensor is a chassis
A wheel is a sensor; a program is an actuator

questions.question: A program contains the command 'turn 90 degrees' twice in different places. What is one benefit of making this a reusable function?
choices: It guarantees the robot's angle sensor is accurate
It can reduce repeated code and make changes easier to manage
It removes the need to test either turn
It changes a conditional into a physical sensor

questions.question: A team wants a robot to stop before crossing a table edge. Which setup best supports that goal?
choices: Use a sound output and a loop that ignores sensor input
Use a wheel encoder alone to identify every table edge
Use a downward-facing sensor and a tested condition that stops motion when an edge is detected
Use a light actuator to estimate distance

questions.question: Why should code be tested with more than one input or situation?
choices: One successful run proves the program handles every condition
Multiple cases make the algorithm harder to understand
Testing can replace defining the intended behavior
Different cases can reveal errors hidden by a single successful run

questions.question: A robot's left and right wheels turn at different speeds to make a curve. Which idea is being applied?
choices: Differential drive control
Image compression
Data encryption
Chemical equilibrium

questions.question: A remote-controlled robot responds only while a person holds a direction button. How does it differ from an autonomous robot?
choices: It must have more sensors than an autonomous robot
It relies on a human operator for movement commands
It cannot use electric motors
It automatically makes every decision from sensor data

questions.question: A program's obstacle sensor reading is sometimes late. Why can a fast robot be less safe than a slow one in the same course?
choices: It receives more accurate readings at higher speed
Its actuators stop before a command is sent
It travels farther before the delayed reading can affect movement
Its algorithm no longer needs conditions

questions.question: A robot arm misses the target because its claw closes before the arm reaches the object. What is the most direct code revision?
choices: Add a second claw-close command at the start
Remove the arm movement command
Change the color of the target
Adjust the sequence or timing so the arm reaches the target before the claw closes
